*Direct literature context could not be pulled due to an API error; the following explanation relies on established pharmacogenomic and biological principles.*

In Chronic Myeloid Leukemia (CML), the reciprocal chromosomal translocation t(9;22)(q34;q11) creates the *BCR-ABL1* fusion oncogene, which encodes a constitutively active tyrosine kinase that drives unregulated leukemic granulocyte proliferation and suppresses apoptosis. Imatinib is a rationally designed, selective small-molecule tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) that functions as an ATP-competitive antagonist, specifically binding to the semi-open, inactive (DFG-out) conformation of the ABL1 kinase domain. By occupying the ATP-binding pocket and stabilizing this inactive state via hydrogen bonds and hydrophobic contacts, Imatinib prevents downstream substrate phosphorylation and interrupts oncogenic signaling pathways (such as STAT5, MAPK, and PI3K/AKT), thereby restoring apoptosis and inducing remission in CML.
